title: Cooktop control board failure
shortDescription: The control board cannot communicate with the cooktop elements.
fullDescription:
Jenn-Air induction cooktops display F0 E0 when the main control board fails internal self-tests or loses signal continuity with the user interface. This is most often caused by power surges, moisture intrusion under the glass, or a defective ribbon connector.

A hard reset (60-minute power-off at the breaker) clears transient faults, but persistent F0 E0 means the control needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop and reseat the UI ribbon connector after confirming power is off.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, replace the main control assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reset fails and you are not comfortable lifting the cooktop.

faq.a: Sometimes. A 5-minute breaker cycle clears transient faults but not hardware failure.

title: User interface communication error
shortDescription: The user interface board has lost communication with the main control.
fullDescription:
F1 E1 indicates the UI (touch glass) is not receiving valid data from the main control. Cause is typically a damaged ribbon cable or failed UI board.

Reset first; if the code returns immediately, suspect the UI board.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop, inspect and reseat the UI ribbon.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not help, the UI board needs replacement.

faq.q: Is the glass safe to touch?
faq.a: Yes when off; this is purely an electronics fault.

title: Cooktop overheated
shortDescription: Internal temperature exceeded safe limit; cooktop entered protection mode.
fullDescription:
F2 E0 occurs when the cooktop sensor detects the induction coil or PCB temperature exceeded the safe threshold. Usually caused by blocked ventilation under the cooktop or use of an undersized pan.

Let the unit cool fully and ensure proper airflow under the countertop.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm cabinet cutout meets spec and vents are unobstructed.

whenToCallPro: If fans run but error returns, the fan or thermistor may need replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air cooktop F2 E0 overheat fix

faq.a: Most often it is a ventilation issue with the cabinet install.

title: Pan not detected or incompatible
shortDescription: Cookware is not magnetic or sized for the active element.
fullDescription:
F3 E0 alerts that the active induction coil cannot detect ferromagnetic cookware. Common with aluminum or copper pans, undersized pots, or warped bottoms.

Use a magnet test: if a magnet sticks firmly to the pan base, it is induction-compatible.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Hold a magnet to the pan base; it must stick strongly.

fixSteps.title: Use proper size
fixSteps.instruction: Match pan diameter to the marked element zone.

whenToCallPro: Not needed unless code persists with confirmed-compatible cookware.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air cooktop F3 E0 pan detection

faq.a: Only magnetic stainless; check with a magnet.

title: Coil temperature sensor open
shortDescription: The thermistor monitoring an induction coil reads open-circuit.
fullDescription:
F4 E0 means a coil thermistor has failed open. The cooktop disables the affected element until the sensor is replaced.

This is a service repair; the coil assembly is removed from beneath the glass.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power at breaker before any service.

fixSteps.title: Service replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop, replace thermistor or coil assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for thermistor replacement under the glass.

faq.q: Can I keep using other zones?
faq.a: Yes, but service should be scheduled promptly.

title: Coil temperature sensor shorted
fullDescription: F4 E1 indicates a shorted thermistor on an induction coil. The element is locked out for safety. Replacement is required.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Schedule replacement of the coil thermistor.

faq.a: Use only unaffected zones until repaired.

title: Touch key stuck
shortDescription: A touch button is sensed continuously pressed.
fullDescription:
F5 E0 appears when a touch key reads pressed for more than ~30 seconds. Usually caused by spills, debris, or a wet cloth resting on the glass.

Clean the surface thoroughly; reset if the code lingers.

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the entire control area dry with a microfiber cloth.

whenToCallPro: Only if cleaning and reset both fail.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air cooktop F5 E0 stuck key

faq.a: Hold the lock key 3 seconds after cleaning.

title: Line voltage out of range
shortDescription: Incoming voltage too high or too low.
fullDescription:
F6 E0 alerts that supply voltage falls outside the 200-250 V operating window. Check breaker, neutral, and verify with a multimeter.

Frequent during brownouts or when shared with high-draw appliances.

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 240 V at the appliance terminal block.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if voltage is out of range.

faq.q: Can I plug into a regular outlet?

title: Cooling fan fault
shortDescription: Internal cooling fan not turning at expected RPM.
fullDescription: F7 E0 is reported when the tach feedback from the internal cooling fan is missing or out of range. Dust buildup or a failing motor are the typical culprits.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop, vacuum dust from fan blades.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning fails, schedule fan replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Jenn-Air cooktop F7 E0 fan fault

faq.q: Can I run without the fan?

title: EEPROM checksum error
shortDescription: Control board memory failed integrity check.
fullDescription:
F9 E0 means the EEPROM on the main control did not pass checksum validation. Often the result of a power-down during firmware update or a degrading control board.

Replace the main board if a power cycle does not clear it.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: If code returns, replace main control board.

whenToCallPro: Recommended unless comfortable with appliance electronics.
